=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text data "des_system_lib std synopsys std_cell_lib des_system_lib dw02 dw01 ramlib ieee;dw01 ieee dw01 dware gtech;dw02 ieee dw02 dware;dw03 std synopsys dware dw03 dw02 dw01 ieee gtech;dw04 dw04 ieee dw01 dware gtech;dw05 dw05 ieee dware;dw06 dw06 ieee dware;dw07 ieee dware;dware ieee dware;gtech ieee gtech;ramlib std ieee;std_cell_lib ieee std_cell_lib;synopsys;"
text tcyc "un-orderable:"
global nst ulong 32
global nln ulong 32
global dep uchar 1024
global indeg ulong 32
global sent uchar 32
global nn ulong 1
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note data lists one library per ;-terminated group: the library, then what it depends on; a library
note that names itself is ignored, as the task asks. Names are kept as (start, length) in data.
note same says whether the names at (a, la) and (b, lb) in data are the same bytes
fn same a ulong la ulong b ulong lb ulong to bool
if ne la lb
ret false
end
for i ulong la
if ne get data add a i get data add b i
ret false
end
end
ret true
end
note before says whether name i sorts before name j, comparing bytes as C's strcmp does
fn before i ulong j ulong to bool
a = get nst i
b = get nst j
la = get nln i
lb = get nln j
for k ulong la
if ge k lb
ret false
end
if ne get data add a k get data add b k
ret lt get data add a k get data add b k
end
end
ret lt la lb
end
note intern returns the number of the name at (s, l), adding it to the table if it is new
fn intern s ulong l ulong to ulong
n = get nn 0
for i ulong n
if same get nst i get nln i s l
ret i
end
end
put nst n s
put nln n l
put nn 0 add n 1
ret n
end
note load reads every group: the first word is the library u, each later word v adds the edge v -> u
fn load to void
first = true
u = ulong 0
st = ulong 0
for i ulong len data
c = get data i
if or eq c 32 eq c 59
if gt i st
v = intern st sub i st
if first
u = v
first = false
else
addedge v u
end
end
st = add i 1
if eq c 59
first = true
end
end
end
end
fn addedge v ulong u ulong to void
if ne v u
if eq get dep add mul v 32 u 0
put dep add mul v 32 u 1
put indeg u add get indeg u 1
end
end
end
fn name i ulong to void
emit part data get nst i get nln i
end
note Kahn's algorithm: output the smallest ready name (in-degree 0), then release what depends on it;
note each round outputs one name, so nn rounds suffice; names never output are part of a cycle
fn main to int
load
n = get nn 0
for r ulong n
b = n
for i ulong n
if and eq get sent i 0 eq get indeg i 0
if eq b n
b = i
else
if before i b
b = i
end
end
end
end
if eq b n
break
end
put sent b 1
if gt r 0
emit sp
end
name b
for j ulong n
if eq get dep add mul b 32 j 1
put indeg j sub get indeg j 1
end
end
end
emit nl
emit tcyc
for i ulong n
if eq get sent i 0
emit sp
name i
end
end
emit nl
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
